rows.abstract: Rationale: Like never before in histroy, mankind is threatened with environmental disasters of global proportions. The environmental cost of the world's economic boom and industrializati on, pursued at a dizzying pace in the last 100 years, is now felt everywhere. Ironically, the current rate of environmental degradation and ecological support systems threatened to totally undo whatever man has gained.< This situation has given to rise to a new field of study called GLOBAL CHANGE, which focusesany changes in the global environment that may alter the capacity of the Earth to sustain life.  Four major issues are currently being addressed  in global change.

rows.abstract: "Landowners Protection Act of 1999". This bill seeks to provide a mandatory period in the relocation  of squatters and to grant tax exemption to illegally occupied residential lands. It also seeks to compensate the landowners in case of failure of the local government unit concerned to act on the request for assistance to evict illegal occupants within the prescribed period.  The foremost intention of this measure is to provide equal protection to the squatters and to the landowners.

rows.abstract: The composition of the governing boards is one determining factor of the SUC's(State Universities and Colleges) success or failure, especially if those sitting in the board are restricted and prevented to effectively carry out his or her duties because of vague and inappropriate provisions presently being provided by R.A. 8292. Most common problem related to the SUC Board is its composition and representation. The student representation in the Board is one perennial issue where questions and opposiations are raised. Another issue is the term of office of the SUC president and the provisions concerning his or her re-appointment.
